data.title: The Ferry Captain's Bet
data.rumour: Captain Ferreira bet she could cross in the fog without radar.
about: Captain Nan Ferreira of the island ferry bet Dewey Lopes $200 she could cross to Gannet Island in the fog without radar, and she's $80 short (§{nanPawn}). She pawns her grandfather's chronometer and asks you to be her witness on deck in the first proper fog.

On the crossing (§{ferrybetDeck}) you can hand her Mott's compass, which always points home, count the bell buoys for her (good odds), keep quiet and let her steer alone (even odds), or take $30 from Dewey to call the buoy wrong. If she wins she buys the chronometer back for $120 (By Dead Reckoning); if she runs aground it's yours to sell (Aground on the Bar). Missing the trip leaves it to chance.
data.notes: Nan lends against her grandfather's chronometer for $80 and buys it back at $120 if she wins.

chronometer.name: Ferreira pocket chronometer
tells: A two-day marine chronometer in a pocket case, still gimballed.
Engraved inside the lid: J. FERREIRA, MASTER, 1951. It's two seconds fast, and has been since 1951.

nanPawn.title: Nan Ferreira needs the stake for her bet

text: Nan Ferreira. I run the island ferry. You'll have heard I bet Dewey Lopes I could cross to Gannet in the fog without radar. I did. I was provoked.
The stake is $200 a side, and I'm eighty short. This was my grandfather's chronometer. He crossed with nothing else for forty years.
$80 against it, and I'll buy it back the day I win. And I need a witness on deck who isn't Dewey's cousin. Midday, this week, first proper fog.

choose.label: Lend her $80 against the chronometer, and be her witness

then.why: Lent Nan Ferreira the stake for her bet

then.text: Good. Wear something warm. And don't touch anything in the wheelhouse.

then.toast: Calendar: the ferry in the fog, at lunch

choose.label: "I don't take bets, Captain. Or lend on them."

then.text: Fair enough. I'll find it somewhere. Dewey's cousin owns a pawnshop in Fall River, but I'd sooner sink.

steps.narrate: Noon, and the fog is so thick the bow is a rumour. The radar has a tea towel over it. Dewey Lopes has a stopwatch and a bag of malasadas.

steps.text: Forty minutes to the Gannet slip, Nan. Not a second over. And no peeking at the phone.
I don't need a phone. I need quiet. Witness, you're on the stern. Tell me when you hear the bell buoy.

hint.then: (it always points the true way home)

then.narrate: The old brass needle swings away from north and settles, steady as a finger, on Gannet Island. Nan looks at it, then at you, and doesn't ask.

then.text: Thirty-eight minutes. I want a recount. I want a different fog.
By dead reckoning, Dewey. Like Grandpa. Witness, I'll be in for the chronometer this afternoon, with interest.

then.why: Nan Ferreira bought back her chronometer

choose.label: Listen hard and count the bell buoys for her

then.narrate: Bell to port. Then the gong on the bar. You call them, she turns on your word, and the slip comes out of the fog dead ahead.

then.text: Thirty-eight minutes. I want a recount. I want a different fog.
By dead reckoning, Dewey. Like Grandpa. Witness, I'll be in for the chronometer this afternoon, with interest.

then.why: Nan Ferreira bought back her chronometer

else.narrate: Bell to port. Or was it starboard? The fog bends sound. You call it, and you're wrong.

else.text: Aground on the bar. In front of Dewey. Grandpa's watch is yours, keeper. A bet's a bet.

choose.label: Keep quiet and let her do it alone

then.narrate: She steers by the clock, the swell and something in her bones. The slip comes out of the fog dead ahead with two minutes to spare.

then.text: Thirty-eight minutes. I want a recount. I want a different fog.
By dead reckoning, Dewey. Like Grandpa. Witness, I'll be in for the chronometer this afternoon, with interest.

then.why: Nan Ferreira bought back her chronometer

else.narrate: She steers by the clock and the swell, and the swell lies. There is a soft long scrape under the hull.

else.text: Aground on the bar. In front of Dewey. Grandpa's watch is yours, keeper. A bet's a bet.

choose.label: Call the bell buoy wrong, on purpose

then.why: Dewey Lopes paid you to call it wrong

then.narrate: "Bell to starboard," you call, and it isn't. There is a soft long scrape under the hull. Dewey finds something very interesting in his malasadas.

then.text: Aground on the bar. In front of Dewey. Grandpa's watch is yours, keeper. A bet's a bet.

mornings.note: you stayed open instead, and she went without a witness

then.why: Nan Ferreira bought back her chronometer

then.toast: Nan Ferreira crossed in the fog and won. She came by early for the chronometer, with interest.

else.toast: Nan Ferreira ran aground on the bar. Her grandfather's chronometer is yours to sell.

epilogue.line: Captain Ferreira still crosses to Gannet in the fog without radar. The Coast Guard has asked her, twice, to stop.
Dewey Lopes framed the newspaper photo of the island ferry aground on the bar. Nan Ferreira has not been into his water taxi since.
